section_c_writing_contract_findings.accepted_script_head: I tried to clean one corner of the workshop. Bad idea. Two minutes in, I found a half-finished 3D print shaped like… I don't know, a bracket? A handle? A mistake with ambition.

quotes: I call for Rivet because last time a "mystery part" turned out to be two experiments welded by optimism.
We line up a reprint, and immediately the perimeter looks… wrong.
cast_presence_drift.interpretation: Rivet is invoked as an active off-screen participant. Patch is nominally the only speaker but the SCENE contains two characters cooperating. For a Patch-only Episode this violates operator expectation — Chris wanted Rivet as part of Patch's world/history (e.g. 'If this gets weird, I'll call Rivet') without being an active participant in the current moment.
cast_presence_drift.root_cause_in_contract: The current long_form writing contract (character_os/writing_contract.py:_INVARIANTS_BLOCK + _NARRATIVE_SHAPES_BLOCK) does NOT restrict cast presence. Nothing in the §4 writing contract tells the model 'this character is the ONLY character in this scene.' The contract treats operator_topic as a subject to explore, not as a scene premise; it explicitly recommends 'story → realization / mistake → lesson / experiment → outcome' shapes that require the character to describe collaborators.

temporal_action_compression.interpretation: The monologue performs an entire mini-experiment from discovery to conclusion. Chris expected ONE moment — discovery + plan + optional condition for later — with future outcomes deferred to a later Episode.
temporal_action_compression.root_cause_in_contract: The long_form contract's _INVARIANTS_BLOCK #4 explicitly demands 'At least one meaningful change… a turn in thought, a piece of tension, an unexpected detail, a reversal.' Combined with _NARRATIVE_SHAPES_BLOCK options ('story → realization', 'observation → explanation', 'mistake → lesson', 'question → exploration → answer'), the contract REWARDS compressing multi-phase arcs into the same script. It does not carry a 'this script depicts one present moment; later outcomes belong in later Episodes' rule.

scene_vs_process_summary.observed: The output reads like 'a narrated experiment / tutorial / retrospective' — past-tense recap of an event ('I tried…', 'I found…') interleaved with plan-forward statements ('Change of plan: … we treat this like an AI memory test').
scene_vs_process_summary.expected_for_solo_episode: 'A character inhabiting a story scene right now' — present-moment framing, no compressed future outcomes, no invented collaborators.
scene_vs_process_summary.root_cause_in_contract: The long_form contract's shape (invariants + narrative-shape menu + CTA policy) is optimized for content-oriented spoken scripts — the historical talking_head use case (short-form talking-head marketing, long-form spoken essays, product explainers). Character OS story-oriented solo dogfood is a genuinely different product mode.

dialogue_contract_contrast.dialogue_frames_output_as_scene: The dialogue_scene contract opens with 'The scene is a conversation between the characters introduced in Section 2… The audience is watching a real exchange, not a pair of parallel presentations.' Dialogue watchability block requires 'ENTER WITH AN IN-SCENE STANCE' and 'PREFER SPECIFIC ACTION / REACTION OVER PHILOSOPHY.' All of that says 'moment', not 'topic'.
dialogue_contract_contrast.talking_head_frames_output_as_topic: The long_form contract opens with 'LENGTH — approximately N seconds of spoken delivery.' Length is the only shape constraint; the rest is about invariants, narrative shape menu, and register. Nothing frames the output as a present-tense scene the character is inhabiting.

section_e_product_mode_classification.verdict: B (mostly the same; Episode-attached talking_head needs a story-mode contract while legacy non-Episode talking_head preserves current content behavior)
rationale: TALKING HEAD AS CONTENT FORMAT (existing, load-bearing): one spokesperson → generated explanatory/promotional/informational speech. Backed by long-form invariants, CTA policy, narrative-shape menu. Every existing caller (marketing scripts, explainers, long-form ad copy) expects these semantics.

SOLO EPISODE AS STORY FORMAT (new dogfood direction): one character → one Episode → one present-moment scene → character-aware + memory-aware → no uncast active participants → no compressing later story outcomes into the same scene.
The two share substrate (spokesperson, K2 retrieval, Universe canon, §10 NarrativeMemory, generate_avatar_speech pipeline) but diverge on writing SEMANTICS.
composition.episode is a natural discriminator that already exists as a field. When set, the caller intended story-mode framing. When null, keep the current content-mode contract.

This mirrors the SESSION 262 pattern: Composition and Episode are already separate; SESSION 262 shipped the FK + attach flow; §11 (potential future slice) would ship the writing-contract discriminator that reads from that FK.

rejected_alternatives.A_small_contract_correction_across_the_b: Would break every legacy talking_head caller — marketing scripts do not want present-moment scene semantics. Rejected: violates §F 'do not break legacy talking_head' constraint.
rejected_alternatives.C_new_recipe: Would duplicate the entire form field surface (spokesperson_picker, script/topic, use_knowledge checkbox, target_duration_seconds, opener, verifier_mode, outro fields). Same infrastructure with different writing contract does not warrant a new recipe when a discriminator field already exists. Also violates the operator's DO-NOT list.
